questions.q: What does Software Composition Analysis (SCA) check?
options: Whether code you wrote matches known vulnerability patterns
Whether third-party and open-source dependencies have known vulnerabilities
Whether a container image uses a non-root user
Whether a secret has been committed to git history
questions.explain: SCA scans manifest and lockfiles and compares dependency versions against databases of known vulnerabilities — it treats your own code as out of scope, since that's SAST's job.

options: A dependency that only exists in production, never in development
A package pulled in indirectly, as a dependency of a dependency you chose directly
A dependency that has been officially deprecated
A dependency written in a different programming language
questions.explain: Transitive dependencies are pulled in indirectly through the packages you do depend on directly, and they can carry vulnerabilities even though you never named them yourself.

questions.q: What are CVE and CVSS used for in dependency scanning?
options: CVE identifies a known vulnerability; CVSS scores its severity for prioritization
CVE and CVSS are two competing container runtimes
CVE is a Kubernetes object; CVSS is a Terraform provider
They are both internal GitHub terms with no external standard meaning
questions.explain: CVE (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) is a standardized identifier for a known vulnerability, and CVSS (Common Vulnerability Scoring System) gives it a numeric severity score.

questions.q: How did Northbridge Retail's platform team find the critical vulnerability in a transitive logging dependency?
options: A developer manually audited every package in the dependency tree
Dependabot's automated scan flagged it as an alert, two layers deep in the tree
A customer reported it after a data breach
It was found during a scheduled annual security audit only
questions.explain: Automated SCA scanning caught the vulnerability in a dependency nobody on the team had chosen directly or audited by hand — manual auditing doesn't scale to a multi-layer dependency tree.

questions.q: Why shouldn't every dependency CVE be treated as equally urgent?
options: Because CVEs expire automatically after 90 days
Because a vulnerability in a function your code never calls carries far less risk than one on a critical execution path
Because CVSS scores are randomly assigned and carry no real meaning
Because Dependabot alerts are always false positives
questions.explain: Severity scores and reachability both matter for triage — a critical CVE in unreachable code is a lower practical priority than a moderate one on a path real traffic hits.
